JUDGMENT
Though matters are listed for admission, with consent of both learned counsel, they are taken up for final disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 05.02.2018 passed by VII Additional District & Sessions Judge, Belagavi, sitting at Chikodi, in MVC No.132/2017, these two appeals are filed by claimant as well as K.S.R.T.C. respectively.
MFA no.100012/2019 is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation and MFA no.103106/2018 is filed by K.S.R.T.C. challenging award on negligence as well as on quantum.

3. Brief facts as stated are that on 05.10.2016, when claimant was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.MH-09/DP-4536 on Gokak- Yaragatti road, a K.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration no.KA-42-F-1165, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against motorcycle and caused accident.
As a result of accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to hospital.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
4. Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition against K.S.R.T.C. (owner of bus) under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Same was contested.
5. After framing issues, tribunal recorded evidence of claimant as PW1 and Dr.Ajit V. Charate as PW2.
Exs. P1
to P13
were marked.

In rebuttal, driver of offending bus was examined as RW1.
6.

On consideration, tribunal held accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver and claimant was entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,96,068/- with interest at 9% per annum and held K.S.R.T.C. liable to pay same.
7. Challenging said award, both claimant as well as K.S.R.T.C. are in appeal.
8. Sri S.C.Bhuti, learned counsel for K.S.R.T.C. submitted that finding of tribunal insofar as negligence was contrary to evidence.
It was submitted that as per Ex.P5 - Motor Vehicles Inspector's report, damages sustained on bus were on front right side and it was a head on collision.

Therefore,
instead of apportioning negligence, tribunal fastened entire liability upon driver of K.S.R.T.C. Said finding called for interference.

The Managing Director vs Shri. Balappa S/O Baburao Talandagi on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15910159/
3 9.
Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that though claimant had stated that his monthly income was Rs.15,000/-, there was no material to substantiate same.
In absence, it had to be assessed notionally, which for year 2016 is Rs.8,750/-.
But tribunal considered monthly income at Rs.9,000/- which was excessive.
It was further submitted that claimant sustained simple fracture.
But tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering which was excessive.
Award of interest at 9% p.a. was also excessive and unjustified.
It was further submitted that though PW2 assessed limb disability at 37%, tribunal considered loss of earning capacity at 12% which was higher and therefore, sought reduction.

10. It was submitted that as per Ex.P5 Motor Vehicles Inspector's report, damages sustained by bus were found on right rear wheel, which would indicate that motor cycle had dashed against bus and therefore, holding entire negligence against corporation driver was unjustified.

11. On other hand, Sri Santosh S.Hattikatagi, learned counsel for claimant submitted that though in Ex.P5 - MVI report found damages on right rear side of bus, as per spot panchanama - Ex.P3 and hand sketch - Ex.P4, accident occurred on extreme right side of road and 2 ft. away from left side edge of motorcycle.
Therefore, bus had traversed on extreme right side at time of accident.
Therefore, there was no substance in challenging on negligence.
12. Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that claimant had stated that his monthly income was Rs.15,000/-p.m.
Therefore, tribunal was justified in considering Rs.9,000/- as monthly income.
It was submitted that claimant had sustained four fractures which was as assessed by PW2 to cause 37% physical disability.
Considering occupation of claimant as power loom operator, same would effect him to higher extent.
Therefore, assessment of functional disability at 12% was inadequate and sought enhancement.
It was submitted that award of compensation towards pain and suffering, attendants, conveyance and incidental charges as well as loss of income during laid up period was inadequate.

Even compensation towards loss of amenities was also on lower side and sought enhancement.
13.

Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and also certified copies of Exs.P3, P4 and P5 made available by learned counsel for K.S.R.T.C.
14.

From above submissions, following points that arise for consideration:-
i) Whether assignment of negligence only against K.S.R.T.C. driver was justified?
ii) Whether assessment of compensation by tribunal calls for modification as sought for?
15. Point no.1:- To establish negligence, claimant produced FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, hand sketch map, MVI report and charge sheet as Exs.P1 to P5 and P7 respectively.
Charge sheet is filed against bus driver.
Ex.P3 - spot panchana and Ex.P4 - hand sketch map would indicate that road at extent spot is running north to south.

Bus was moving towards Yaragatti form Gokak from, i.e.
south to north.
Motorcycle was coming from opposite direction.
Accident spot is 2 ft. away from The Managing Director vs Shri.

Balappa S/O Baburao Talandagi on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15910159/
4 eastern edge of road.
Same would indicate that bus had gone on its wrong side and caused accident.
In view of above, finding of tribunal regarding entire negligence against bus driver would not call for interference.

Hence, point no.1 is answered in 'affirmative'.
16. Point no.2
- Insofar as monthly income, though claimant stated that he was earning - 10 - Rs.15,000/- per month, same was not substantiated.
In absence of specific evidence, it has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2016 is Rs.8,750/-.
Therefore, tribunal was not justified in taking monthly income as Rs.9,000/-.

17. Insofar as physical disability, as per PW2 - Dr.Ajit V.Charate, claimant sustained fracture of right lower end of ulna, compound fracture upper end 2, 3, 4, 5, metacarpals, compound (R) fracture of right lower end femur and fracture of upper tibia at right leg.

After examining claimant, he has issued disability certificate - Ex.P9, wherein it is stated that there is malunited fracture of right supracondylar femur, malunited fracture of right distal ulna, ununited fracture of 3rd, 4th and 5th metacarapal of right hand.
He assessed limb disability of 37%.

Considering disability noted and effect of nonunion of metacarpal fractures,
- 11 - assessment of functional disability at 12% to whole body would not be justified.
It would be appropriate to consider it as 18%.

Thus, future loss of income would be Rs.8,750/- X 18% X 12 X 17 = Rs.3,21,300/-
18.
Claimant sustained four fractures.
Tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Considering number of fractures and period of treatment, compensation towards pain and suffering would not be adequate.
It would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.80,000/-.
Tribunal awarded Rs.57,748/- towards medical expenses which is in complete reimbursement of bills produced.
Therefore, no enhancement is called for.
Claimant has taken inpatient treatment for a period of 21 days.
Therefore, award of Rs.5,000/- towards nourishment and Rs.5,000/- towards attendant and conveyance etc. would not be justified.
It would be appropriate to award a sum - 12 - of Rs.15,000/- together.
Normally, fractures take about three months to heal.

Therefore, loss of income during laid up period has to be assessed for three months i.e. Rs.8,750/- X 3 =Rs.26,250/-.
19.
Considering disability sustained, award of compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness would be inadequate.
It would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.60,000/-.

 3.

 up period  6. Loss of amenities 60,000/-

Insofar as rate of interest, this Court in case of SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. LAXMI reported in 2018(4) AKR 808 held that interest payable on award under Motor Vehicles Act would be as per Section 34 of Code of Civil Procedure i.e. at 6%.

award of interest in excess of same would not be tenable.
Thus, point no.2 is answered 'partly in affirmative' as above.
2. Consequently, I pass following:
ORDER i) Appeals are allowed in part.

ii) Judgment and award dated 05.02.2018 passed by VII Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Belagavi, Sitting at Chikodi, in MVC No.132/2017 is modified by enhancing compensation to - 14 - Rs.5,59,998/- from Rs.3,96,068/- with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till date of deposit.
